Figures are arithmetic on public numbers, never achievable value.

arguments.value: PARTLY CONFIRMED, with the observability boundary precisely mapped. The frozen rule selected constraint group SSE-SP, 2026-05-18..31 (right-censored by the window): 8,259 repeat-curtailment cycles consistent with RRT, 69,869 MWh storage bid-down. The observable sequence reconstructs at scale (excerpt day 2026-05-20: 1,060 cycles; focus unit E_DOLLB-1: 21 cycles, 88 distinct acceptances in one day, repeatedly instructed from scheduled export through zero to around -99 MW import, NONE SO-flagged in the public record). Two links are NOT publicly observable and are the finding: (1) the intraday re-sale that turns repetition into re-trading; (2) the unit-to-constraint-group mapping that would localise money to the boundary. No figure is a cost of RRT; concurrency is observed, substitution never asserted.

arguments.value: CORRECTION AND STRENGTHENING of fnd-003-episode-reconstructed (which remains on the record as published). (1) Attribution: the frozen selection rule scores an episode by counting repeat-curtailment cycles across the entire declared GB storage universe over the episode dates; no constraint-group filter was declared and none is publicly implementable - the missing unit-to-group mapping the original finding itself identified. The 8,259 cycles and 69,869 MWh are GB-wide storage activity concurrent with the SSE-SP episode dates and must not be presented as activity behind SSE-SP. (2) Methodology alignment, from the pinned Ofgem RRT policy paper (June 2026, art-003-ofgem-rrt-paper): NESO estimates the balancing cost impact of RRT from storage at approximately GBP 99m in FY 2025/26 (12-hour search window), up from approximately GBP 64m in FY 2024/25, with pumped storage around 80 percent of the two-year total; the methodology counts only settlement periods with a positive FPN, a SYSTEM-FLAGGED bid acceptance, and a subsequent net-upward PN revision within a 3/6/12-hour horizon - computed from timestamped PN revision history that is not public (only final PN vintages are). (3) Descriptive tally over the episode dates (evidence: so-flag-tally.json): 90,020 distinct storage-unit acceptances GB-wide, of which 2,904 (3.2 percent) are SO-flagged; focus unit E_DOLLB-1 recorded 1,492 acceptances with zero SO-flagged, so its 21 excerpt-day cycles cannot be presented as a demonstrated constraint-driven RRT example. Consequence: the repeat-curtailment score is a concurrence signature, not NESO's RRT count, and the public record cannot reproduce NESO's RRT diagnosis - the missing inputs are point-in-time PN revision history and authoritative constraint attribution.

arguments.value: PARTLY EXPLAINED, with the observability boundary where the declaration predicted it. The frozen rule selected 2026-06-24 p42 (Constraints GBP1,176,150), which falls inside the 19:00-22:00 window NESO had warned about the previous night and CANCELLED at 13:20; all four of June's dearest half-hours fall inside it. NESO's own notice supplies the bridge: 1,250-1,300 MW of generation was excluded from available system margin BY SYSTEM CONSTRAINTS, against a 1,450-1,900 MW shortfall. At the window's open the dispatchable fleet was at published limits (CCGT headroom 88 MW; pumped storage, nuclear and non-pumped hydro zero). Through the peak the record shows 1,085 MWh of accepted bids across 113 units with ZERO accepted offers, pumped storage held at 0 against a 150 MW schedule, and the large positive money OUTSIDE the BM (GBP1,277,241 over 1,173 MWh, all classified Energy) while BM cashflow is negative. Not determinable from public data: why the Constraints series peaks in p42 rather than p41 where BSAD peaks; the Peterhead gap between ~729 MW metered and ~1,150 MW instructed; and whether the generation NESO excluded from margin is the generation visible being bid down. No transmission boundary is named.
